findings.defect: The skip pass rewrites the manifest with only the not-yet-delivered jobs, but `--request-id ID` names entry *n* `ID-n` (C-17.7) and a repeated request id with a different payload digest is exit 2, not a fresh job (C-6.2). Filtering shifts every surviving entry's index.
findings.failure_scenario: First run submits [A,B,C] as ID-0/ID-1/ID-2. A finishes and writes its out file. The workflow is relaunched with the same requestId: the skip pass drops A, so the manifest is [B,C] and B is submitted as ID-0 (A's digest) and C as ID-1 (B's digest). Both collide with a different digest, so both are refused with rc 2 and nothing is resubmitted — the documented idempotent path is precisely the one that never recovers the unfinished work.
findings.fix: Keep the index stable: submit the full manifest every time and let C-6.2 dedupe the already-created entries (same digest returns the existing job id, created=false), using the skip list only to label those entries in the report. If items must be dropped, pad the manifest so each item keeps its original index, or drop `--batch` for the retry path and submit per item with a name-derived request id.

findings.defect: Step 1 truncates the job-id file (`open(F['jobs'],'w').close()`) and redirects `run --batch` over `submit.jsonl` with `>` before the ids are safely recorded; those two files are the only record of what was submitted, and step 1 has no guard against running a second time.
findings.failure_scenario: The step 1 Bash call is killed (or the agent re-issues it after any hiccup) after `subfleet run --batch` has already returned ids. Without `--request-id` the resubmission creates a second set of jobs for the same work, and the first set's ids are gone: submit.jsonl was overwritten and jobs.txt was emptied. Step 2 then waits on the wrong ids, and line 217 tells the user to inspect `${stateDir}/${files.jobs}`, which the same step just truncated.
findings.fix: Make step 1 refuse to resubmit when state exists: `if [ -s jobs.txt ]; then echo ALREADY_SUBMITTED; ... fi`. Append submissions to a timestamp/attempt-suffixed jsonl rather than `>`-ing one file, derive jobs.txt from the union of all submit files, and only truncate after the ids have been parsed out.

findings.defect: The loop-continue rule keys on `WAIT_RC=124`, but `wait` exits with the max over all requested jobs (subfleet/cli.py:1033-1048): a lost job is 125 and a cancelled one 130, both greater than the 124 contributed by pending jobs.
findings.failure_scenario: Ten jobs are submitted; one is cancelled early and nine are still queued. The first slice exits 130, the dispatcher reads 'Any other WAIT_RC: done' and stops after one loop. The nine jobs printed PENDING lines, which the prompt only assigns a state for 'after ${MAX_WAIT_LOOPS} calls', so the model either invents states or omits the names entirely and the workflow reports them as unreported while the jobs keep running in the daemon.
findings.fix: Drive the loop off the data, not the exit code: have the step 2 python print a single `PENDING_COUNT=n` line and instruct the agent to repeat while PENDING_COUNT > 0 (and to treat any PENDING line as state running/rc 124 whenever the loop ends, for any reason).

findings.defect: `cd ${q(stateDir)} && cat > …` guards only the `cat`; the following lines of the same Bash call run regardless of whether the cd succeeded, and nothing ever creates stateDir. The count test `[ "$(python3 -c …)" -gt 0 ]` then compares an empty string and returns non-zero, falling into the else branch.
findings.failure_scenario: stateDir (defaulted to the dirname of items[0].outPath) does not exist yet. The cd fails, the manifest is never written, the skip python tracebacks to stderr, the count test errors, and the call's final output is `SUBMIT_RC=0` / `NOTHING_TO_SUBMIT`. The dispatcher reports a clean run with zero jobs and the workflow returns a success-shaped summary for a batch that was never submitted.
findings.fix: Start step 1 with `mkdir -p DIR && cd DIR || { echo SUBMIT_RC=1; echo STATE_DIR_FAILED; exit 1; }` and make the count explicit, e.g. `n=$(python3 -c … 2>/dev/null || echo -1); if [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; then … elif [ "$n" -lt 0 ]; then echo MANIFEST_UNREADABLE; …`.

findings.defect: The prompt defines a per-name mapping only for SKIP, REFUSED and DONE lines, yet the schema requires one entry per name with `state` drawn from a closed enum and integer `rc`/`out_bytes`. Several reachable outcomes produce a name with none of those lines.
findings.failure_scenario: `run --batch` exits 2 on a client-side check (C-17.7: nothing is submitted and the message goes to stderr), so submit.jsonl is empty: no SKIP, no SUBMITTED, no REFUSED. The agent is told to 'report with wait_loops 0' but has no rule for the job entries, and schema validation forbids omitting them, so a Haiku model fills in plausible values — most likely state 'failed' rc 0 or state 'succeeded' — and the workflow's summary counts them as real outcomes.
findings.fix: Add an 'unknown' member to the state enum and one explicit sentence: 'A name with no SKIP, REFUSED or DONE line is state "unknown", job_id "", rc -1, out_bytes 0, notes = the stderr tail or the marker that was missing.' Also print the submit stderr tail in the no-SUBMITTED path so notes has something to carry.

findings.defect: All state filenames are derived from `label` alone (default 'fanout') and stateDir defaults to the output directory of items[0], so two fanouts writing into the same directory share submit.jsonl, jobs.txt and wait.jsonl.
findings.failure_scenario: The main session launches two subfleet-fanout workflows over the same output directory without passing label/stateDir. The second dispatcher's step 1 truncates jobs.txt and overwrites submit.jsonl while the first dispatcher is mid-wait; the first's next slice runs `subfleet wait $(cat jobs.txt)` on the other batch's ids, reports those jobs' states under its own names, and its own job ids are unrecoverable.
findings.fix: Fold requestId (or a required unique label) into the filenames, and make step 1 abort with a marker line when jobs.txt already exists and is non-empty for a different batch. Defaulting `label` to 'fanout' while also defaulting stateDir to a shared directory should not be possible at once — require an explicit label when stateDir is not given.

findings.defect: Both steps are multi-line blocks containing two or three heredocs whose terminators must land unindented on their own lines, and the entire manifest JSON (pretty-printed, up to 256 entries) is inlined into the prompt for the model to retype verbatim.
findings.failure_scenario: A Haiku model re-indents the python body to line up under the `if`, drops a blank line, or renders `SUBFLEET_FANOUT_EOF` with leading whitespace. The heredoc never terminates and swallows the remainder of the command, so the Bash call hangs to its 600 s cap with no SUBMIT_RC line; or it silently mangles one manifest path, and that job runs against the wrong workdir/out. For a large batch the prompt is also dominated by JSON the model must reproduce character-for-character.
findings.fix: Remove the line-structure dependency: emit the manifest with `JSON.stringify(manifest)` (one line) written via `printf '%s' <single-quoted json> > file`, and collapse each python snippet into a `python3 -c` argument quoted with `q()` (the quoting helper already handles embedded quotes), or write the snippets to `.py` files in a one-off first call and have steps 1 and 2 be single short command lines.

findings.defect: `out_bytes` on DONE lines is taken from the wait object's `out_path`, but `wait --json` emits the daemon's job row and the deliverable is resolved elsewhere as `_artifact_path(job,'deliverable') or job.get('out_path')` (subfleet/cli.py:1268,1280), so `out_path` can be absent or null for a job that did deliver.
findings.failure_scenario: A job succeeds and writes its deliverable; the wait row carries no usable out_path, so the python reports `out_bytes=0`, the agent copies it, and the workflow's caller sees a succeeded job with an apparently empty output and re-runs it.
findings.fix: The python already has the full manifest in F['all']; build a job_id/name -> out map from it and fall back to that path when `o.get('out_path')` is missing, e.g. `out = o.get('out_path') or outs.get(name)`.
